chapter_notes.single_objective_concentration: Objective 38 ('Skin and integument conditions') is by far the dominant MCC anchor in this chapter (39 of 41 OBJECTIVE_REFERENCE citations), reflecting that MCC's Medical Expert framework has exactly one broad, presentation-oriented objective covering the full breadth of dermatologic diagnoses - most named Toronto Notes diagnoses in this chapter map as COMPONENT of objective 38 rather than DIRECT, per CLAUDE.md's guidance that the presentation-oriented framework means many diagnoses legitimately map as components of broader objectives rather than each earning its own DIRECT mapping. A minority of units earned DIRECT status either because the objective's causal_conditions/rationale text names the diagnosis or category explicitly and unambiguously (e.g., 'Malignant (e.g., melanoma)' for SU-D-36; 'Hair presentations - Alopecia...Hypertrichosis' verbatim for SU-D-38) or because a dedicated MCC objective exists for the exact presentation (Pruritus=85 for SU-D-43; Urticaria/angioedema=97-2 for SU-D-42).
chapter_notes.no_weak_mappings: Zero WEAK mapping_strength citations in this chapter - every mcc_evidence citation achieved at least MODERATE strength, so no unit required requires_scope_review flagging on mapping-quality grounds.
chapter_notes.toc_structural_quality: Chapter D's TOC page (pdf 189) is a two-column layout that OCR'd with adjacent-column text interleaved onto single lines, producing garbled multi-topic node titles for roughly 20 of the chapter's 42 toc_inventory.json nodes and causing 7 real headings to receive no node at all (see study_units.json's same_page_merge_resolutions and unresolved_heading_resolution fields, and research/scope/chapters/D/review_items.json for the informational review-queue entries). This is a substantially higher merge/drop rate than the pilot chapters (C, ELOM) or A/CP, reflecting genuinely worse source OCR quality for this specific chapter rather than a methodology change.
